items.title: Charles Calello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2025
items.q: my father, although he played club dates, had Miles Davis records in his collection. So as a kid I found them and I was sort of impressed over the fact that this music was appealing to me.

ctx.x: Yeah. And how would you know to play [scats], just that like was inside you from listening to the radio or something?

Well my father was a musician, and I studied trumpet for a while. But my father wanted me to become an accordion player because the accordion players worked at bar mitzvahs and weddings and they always got paid extra because they worked extra hours or something. So my father wanted me to play the accordion. So I had knowledge of music from a very early age and my father, although he played club dates, had Miles Davis records in his collection. So as a kid I found them and I was sort of impressed over the fact…
also writing – in school we were writing figured bass. So I had some knowledge as to, you know, what to do. But these were head arrangements. I wasn’t writing anything out.
